title: Adaptive tail suppressor + hotpath probe to cut tracing overhead
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Tracer instrumentation and span serialization on the inference hotpath contributes measurable allocation and CPU pressure under high QPS, leading to p50/p95 token-latency regression spikes during bursty traffic. Current route-level sampling and reservoir approaches are effective but still incur hotpath cost for prefiltering and exemplarization.

Goal: Implement an adaptive 'tail suppressor' that reduces hotpath tracing work during detected high-throughput/tail-risk windows while preserving fidelity for errors and rare long-tail requests. Complement this with a lightweight hotpath probe that measures realtime sampling cost and triggers conservative sampling adjustments automatically.

High-level approach:
- Add a tiny probe hook at ingress that measures per-request tracing overhead (micro-timer + cheap counters) and reports aggregated stats to the sampling controller off-hotpath.
- Implement an adaptive sampling controller (sidecar/ingress proxy-level) that changes sampling parameters (probability, reservoir size, exemplarization) per-route and per-tenant using a sliding-window of observed overhead and tail probability signals.
- Move expensive span encoding/attribute enrichment off the hotpath: hotpath emits a compact envelope with a sampling hint; full enrichment and JSON/OTLP encoding is performed asynchronously by background workers when a span is selected for retention.
- Maintain strong guarantees for errors/high-severity traces via a small synchronous micro-reservoir and deterministic retention for spans that meet severity predicates (errors, high-latency without backoff).

Deliverables:
- ingress probe + aggregation API
- adaptive sampling controller implementation and config knobs
- async span enricher/encoder worker
- dashboards and alerts (sampling cost, retained error rate, trace fidelity)
- canary rollout plan and feature-flag toggle

Why different from previous work: Prior tickets focused on prefilter or reservoir algorithms. This ticket ties a real-time overhead probe to a control loop that actively suppresses nonessential tracing work, and decouples encoding to eliminate allocations from the hotpath.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath CPU and allocation attributable to tracing reduced by >=40% in 95th percentile under 10k qps synthetic load
Error traces for 500ms+ requests are still retained at >= 98% (measured over 24h of production traffic)
New sampling controller exposes per-route knobs and auto-adjusts based on probe signals; behavior documented in Confluence
Async span encoder reduces median trace emission latency (time spent on hotpath) to <100us per request
Canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) executed with no increase in user-facing error rates; rollback documented and tested
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind sampling.experimental.enable flag. 1) Deploy probe + controller in staging, run 24h smoke harness 2) Canary at 5% traffic for 4 hours, observe tracing cost and error retention dashboards 3) Ramp to 25% for 24h, check fidelity metrics and SLOs 4) Full rollout with monitoring playbook. Automatic rollback if retained-error-rate drops below 95% or if tracing CPU exceeds baseline+15%
risks: Debugging visibility reduction if sampling heuristics are mis-tuned (mitigation: short-term 'always-on' debug bucket and on-demand full-trace capture via feature flag)
Edge case where async encoder fails and selected spans are lost (mitigation: at-least-once retry + dead-letter queue + alerting)
Potential tenant-level compliance concerns for regulated customers if retention heuristics drop traces (mitigation: per-tenant opt-out and ability to pin deterministic retention)
Controller oscillation under very bursty traffic (mitigation: hysteresis and conservative backoff in control loop)
